chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yahya ibn Bashir, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who intends Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with the little of his deeds, Allah will manifest for him more than what he intended; and the one who intends the people with the much of his deeds, through the exhaustion of his body and the wakefulness of his night, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will refuse except that He belittles it in the eyes of those who hear him.

key_terms.يُقَلِّلَهُ: He belittles it / makes it small

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sincerity and showing-off in Islamic worship according to hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a cornerstone of Shia spiritual psychology, distinguishing between the internal purity of intention (ikhlas) and the external corruption of seeking human validation (riya'). It highlights the divine mechanism where Allah amplifies the spiritual weight of minor deeds done sincerely, while simultaneously diminishing the perceived value of abundant deeds done for show, thereby warning believers that the audience of the masses is less reliable than the Audience of Allah.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yahya Bin Bashir, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who intends Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic with the little from his deeds, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Manifest a lot for him from what he intended; and the one who intends the people with the more from his deeds during the exhaustion from his body and staying awake from his night, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Refuse except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Belittles it in the eyes of the ones whom he (intended to) hear him’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Yahya ibn Bashir from his father from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Whoever wants Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, with a small deed Allah uncovers for him a reward bigger than what he wanted. Whoever wants people with a great deal of deeds, physical effort, and with, nightly vigil, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, deems it necessary to belittle it (his effort) in the eyes of those for whom they (the deeds) were meant to be.”
